AI.result: The exterior metric correction is Yukawa-suppressed (e^{-r/λ}), non-analytic in coupling; Schwarzschild-like light bending (4GM/b) holds exactly at leading order; first correction is λ^{-1/2}b^{-3/2}e^{-b/λ}, confirmed numerically (~20% error at b=4λ, ~7% at b=12λ); black holes have zero scalar charge, neutron stars acquire pressure-weighted scalar charge; weak lensing cannot discriminate the theory, but strong-field photon sphere imaging and EoS-dependent interior structure can.
AI.conclusion: Quadratic f(R) gravity predicts a qualitative (not merely quantitative) distinction between black holes and neutron stars: the former are 'GR-mimickers' in lensing, the latter deviate via pressure-coupled scalar hair. Discrimination requires strong-field observations (photon ring) or nuclear-EoS-sensitive probes, not weak-lensing expansion techniques.

title: CFT characters from localization
summary: We explain a general procedure to compute characters of chiral algebras of 2d (S)CFTs geometrically from their coadjoint orbits, in analogy with the coadjoint orbit method for finite-dimensional Lie groups. We demonstrate that this method can be used to give concise rederivations of the characters of the Virasoro algebra, Kac-Moody algebras, as well as supersymmetric generalizations.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a geometric method—based on coadjoint orbits—to compute characters of chiral algebras in 2D (S)CFTs, recovering known results for Virasoro, Kac–Moody, and their supersymmetric extensions concisely.
AI.motivation: To develop a geometric, orbit-based framework for computing characters of infinite-dimensional chiral algebras in 2D conformal field theories, inspired by the finite-dimensional coadjoint orbit method in representation theory.
AI.method: Applies the coadjoint orbit method to the infinite-dimensional Lie algebras underlying chiral symmetry—specifically the Virasoro and Kac–Moody algebras and their supersymmetric extensions—by identifying appropriate coadjoint orbits and computing associated geometric quantization data (e.g., symplectic volumes or index-theoretic invariants) yielding characters.
AI.result: Recovers the standard characters of the Virasoro algebra (including the Cardy formula in certain limits), affine Kac–Moody algebras, and their N=1/N=2 superconformal counterparts, all via unified geometric reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The coadjoint orbit method extends naturally to infinite-dimensional chiral algebras of 2D CFTs, providing a powerful geometric unification and simplification of character computations, with potential applications to modular invariance, holography, and classification of rational CFTs.

title: Stability of Collective Neutrino Oscillations -- A Distributional Approach
summary: We study the stability of collective neutrino oscillations using a distributional approach motivated by the statistical mechanics of Kuramoto synchronization. Treating the ensemble of neutrino flavor polarization vectors in the thermodynamic limit $N\to\infty$, we derive an exact nonlinear Fokker--Planck (continuity) equation for the one-body distribution $F(\vec{\mathbf{S}},ω,t)$ on the flavor sphere. This equation admits a two-parameter family of azimuthally symmetric stationary solutions, whose stability we analyze by linearizing around them. The resulting eigenvalue condition determines the growth or decay rate of small perturbations from \emph{any} initial distribution -- not merely from a state close to full flavor coherence -- thereby going significantly beyond the conventional linear stability analysis of collective modes. In special limits the condition reproduces known synchronization thresholds in the two-beam model, providing a non-trivial check of the framework. We present analytical results for the eigenvalue equation and explore stability phase diagrams for physically relevant frequency distributions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a distributional approach inspired by Kuramoto synchronization to study collective neutrino oscillation stability, deriving an exact nonlinear Fokker–Planck equation for the flavor polarization distribution and performing a generalized linear stability analysis beyond conventional coherent-state approximations.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of conventional linear stability analyses—which assume perturbations near fully coherent states—by developing a framework capable of assessing stability against arbitrary initial distributions, grounded in statistical mechanics analogies to synchronization.
AI.method: Derives an exact nonlinear Fokker–Planck (continuity) equation for the one-body distribution $F(\vec{\mathbf{S}}, \omega, t)$ on the flavor sphere in the thermodynamic limit; performs linear stability analysis around azimuthally symmetric stationary solutions; obtains an eigenvalue condition governing perturbation growth/decay for generic initial distributions.
AI.result: A general eigenvalue condition determining stability of collective neutrino oscillations for arbitrary initial distributions; analytical solutions to the eigenvalue equation; stability phase diagrams for physically relevant frequency spectra; recovery of known two-beam synchronization thresholds in limiting cases as validation.
AI.conclusion: The distributional framework significantly extends collective neutrino oscillation stability theory beyond the standard coherent-mode approximation, enabling robust, first-principles assessment of instability onset across broad classes of spectral and angular configurations.

title: On Quasiparticles within the Refined Gribov-Zwanziger Model
summary: The problem of the effective excitations of a gauge theory in the nonperturbative regime remains not completely understood. Using the Refined Gribov-Zwanziger (RGZ) theory as effective model for pure gauge Yang-Mills theories, we revisit the quasiparticle (quadratic) excitations of the theory. A novel interpretation of such quasiparticles is proposed, in the case of real mass poles, taking into account the manifest ${\cal PT}-$symmetry of the RGZ Lagrangian.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines quasiparticle excitations in pure Yang-Mills theory using the Refined Gribov-Zwanziger (RGZ) framework, proposing a new interpretation grounded in the manifest PT-symmetry of the RGZ Lagrangian for real-mass poles.
AI.motivation: To better understand nonperturbative effective excitations in gauge theories, particularly where standard perturbative approaches fail.
AI.method: Application and reinterpretation of the Refined Gribov-Zwanziger (RGZ) effective model for pure gauge Yang-Mills theories, with emphasis on PT-symmetry analysis of quadratic (quasiparticle) excitations.
AI.result: A novel PT-symmetric interpretation of real-mass-pole quasiparticles in the RGZ framework is established, offering a refined physical understanding of nonperturbative excitations.
AI.conclusion: The manifest PT-symmetry of the RGZ Lagrangian provides a physically meaningful basis for interpreting real-mass quasiparticles as effective excitations, advancing the conceptual foundation of nonperturbative Yang-Mills dynamics.

title: From Nonmetricity Operators to the Physical Spectrum: A Branch-Complete Analysis of Local Four-Derivative Symmetric Teleparallel Gravity
summary: We develop a branch-complete classical free-spectrum analysis of local parity-even symmetric teleparallel gravity containing all pure-gravity nonmetricity operators through four derivatives. After canonicalisation and integration by parts, the nonlinear action contains 116 independent operators distributed as $5+13+29+69$ among $Q^2$, $(\nabla Q)^2$, $Q^2\nabla Q$ and $Q^4$. Around Minkowski spacetime in the coincident gauge only the first two sectors contribute to the quadratic action, which reduces to four two-derivative and five four-derivative bilinears. We map the original coefficients to this nine-dimensional basis, construct the Hessian and momentum kernel, and classify local linear gauge symmetries. Unrestricted linearised diffeomorphism invariance imposes six independent relations and leaves a three-parameter family $(A,B,C)$. We also recover TDiff, Weyl, WTDiff and additional accidental symmetry branches. Barnes--Rivers decomposition, gauge fixing, exact inversion and conserved-source saturation reduce the physical exchange to spin-two and scalar factors $A+2Cq$ and $2A+(3B-2C)q$. The generic regular spectrum contains a massless graviton, a massive spin-two state and a massive scalar, with eight degrees of freedom. The massive spin-two residue is necessarily opposite to that of the healthy massless graviton. The regular classification leaves only GR/STEGR, $A>0$ with $B=C=0$, and the scalar extension, $A>0$, $B>0$, $C=0$, as fully healthy Minkowski loci. The latter has three degrees of freedom and mixed ultraviolet behaviour, with tensor exchange scaling as $k^{-2}$ and scalar exchange as $k^{-4}$. Thus, within this finite local metric theory, full four-derivative tensor suppression requires the finite massive spin-two pole with opposite residue.

AI.tldr: This paper performs a complete free-spectrum analysis of parity-even symmetric teleparallel gravity up to four derivatives in nonmetricity Q, identifying 116 independent operators; around Minkowski in the coincident gauge, only 9 quadratic terms survive; linearised diffeomorphism invariance reduces the parameter space to three constants (A,B,C); spectral analysis reveals generically 8 degrees of freedom (massless graviton + massive spin-2 + massive scalar), with the massive spin-2 necessarily having opposite residue; only two cases — GR/STEGR and a scalar-extended version — are fully healthy (ghost- and tachyon-free) on Minkowski.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify the linearised spectrum and consistency conditions (ghosts, tachyons, gauge symmetries) of local, parity-even, symmetric teleparallel gravity theories built from nonmetricity up to quartic order, thereby identifying viable alternatives to General Relativity within the teleparallel framework.
AI.method: Branch-complete free-spectrum analysis: canonicalisation of the full nonlinear action (116 independent nonmetricity operators up to Q⁴); expansion around Minkowski in coincident gauge; identification of quadratic Lagrangian (9 bilinears); construction of Hessian and momentum-space kernel; Barnes–Rivers decomposition of nonmetricity; gauge fixing and exact inversion of kinetic operator; conserved-source saturation to extract physical propagators; classification of linear gauge symmetries (Diff, TDiff, Weyl, WTDiff, accidental).
AI.result: Generic theory has 8 degrees of freedom: massless spin-2 (residue +1), massive spin-2 (residue −1), and massive scalar; linearised diffeomorphism invariance imposes six constraints, leaving three free parameters (A,B,C); only two subcases are fully healthy on Minkowski: (i) GR/STEGR with A>0, B=C=0 (2 DOF), and (ii) scalar extension with A>0, B>0, C=0 (3 DOF, mixed UV scaling: k⁻² for tensor, k⁻⁴ for scalar).
AI.conclusion: Within local, parity-even, symmetric teleparallel gravity up to four derivatives, full ghost-free, tachyon-free propagation on Minkowski spacetime is highly constrained: only GR/STEGR and its minimal scalar extension satisfy all consistency requirements; the presence of a finite massive spin-two pole with negative residue is necessary for complete tensor-sector UV suppression, ruling out generic higher-derivative extensions.

title: Chaos is Target-Blind in High-Energy QCD Evolution
summary: Chaotic evolution measures how rapidly nearby configurations separate, but the existence of such rapid evolution does not by itself determine what physical information the evolution actually carries. For fixed-coupling JIMWLK evolution with fresh transverse-local, color-isotropic noise, we show that this distinction becomes exact - leading to a no go theorem. At finite rapidity step and finite transverse regulator, the exact linearized update depends on the Wilson-line background only through local adjoint rotations of fresh color-isotropic noise. Once the past is conditioned upon, these rotations leave the complete local noise measure invariant, so the tangent process has the same probability law for any target ensemble evolved with the same regulated fixed-coupling dynamics, including dilute and saturated ensembles. After the exact global color-rotation mode is removed, the reduced tangent process found to have a positive leading Lyapunov exponent which indicate chaotic evolution. Fixed-coupling JIMWLK therefor can be dynamically chaotic while its tangent-only statistics carry no information about the target ensemble. Spatially nonlocal noise however evades the argument because correlations between distinct sites leave relative Wilson lines in the conditional covariance.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a 'no-go' theorem for fixed-coupling JIMWLK evolution: although the dynamics is mathematically chaotic (positive Lyapunov exponent), the tangent-space statistics are universal—identical for all target ensembles (dilute or saturated)—because local color rotations of isotropic noise preserve the conditional noise measure; spatially nonlocal noise breaks this universality.
AI.motivation: To clarify whether chaotic evolution in high-energy QCD (specifically JIMWLK) encodes physical information about the target ensemble, distinguishing mathematical chaos from physically informative sensitivity.
AI.method: Analytical analysis of linearized (tangent) JIMWLK evolution under fixed coupling, with transverse-local, color-isotropic noise; examination of conditional noise measure invariance under local adjoint rotations; decomposition to isolate global color-rotation mode; Lyapunov exponent computation for the reduced tangent process; contrast with spatially nonlocal noise case.
AI.result: Exact invariance of the tangent-process probability law across all target ensembles under regulated fixed-coupling JIMWLK with local isotropic noise; emergence of positive leading Lyapunov exponent only after removing the trivial global color-rotation mode; breakdown of universality when noise is spatially nonlocal due to Wilson-line–dependent conditional covariance.
AI.conclusion: Fixed-coupling JIMWLK exhibits dynamical chaos without ensemble-discriminative tangent statistics — chaos is 'blind' to target structure under local noise; thus, chaos alone does not imply physical information content, and nonlocal noise is required for ensemble-sensitive stochastic dynamics.

title: Flavor Tomography of Long-Lived Neutrino-Mass Mediators: Probing the Neutrino Mass Ordering at the HL-LHC
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, this paper is accepted by Chinese Phys. C
summary: The neutrino mass ordering remains unresolved because long-baseline oscillation measurements are entangled with the unknown CP phase $δ_{CP}$; a collider probe free of this degeneracy would provide a qualitatively different, complementary test. We show that when the long-lived charged particle producing a displaced-lepton signal at the High-Luminosity LHC is also the mediator responsible for Majorana neutrino masses---the \textit{shared-coupling condition}---the Casas--Ibarra parametrization determines the lepton flavor ratio $N_e/N_μ$ of time-delayed leptons in terms of Pontecorvo--Maki--Nakagawa--Sakata (PMNS) mixing parameters alone. Within the resulting \textit{shared-coupling class} of models the ratio is fixed by oscillation data, independent of all beyond-Standard-Model mass and coupling parameters up to calculable corrections bounded by charged-lepton-flavor-violation data, yielding $N_e/N_μ= 0.140$ for the Normal and $2.11$ for the Inverted Hierarchy---a separation of more than an order of magnitude between the two predictions. This prediction holds identically across the Scotogenic model, the Type-III seesaw, the inverse and linear seesaw, and lepton-portal dark matter, and is stable against oscillation-parameter uncertainties and detector-efficiency variations, which cancel in the ratio. A single efficiency-corrected decision criterion identifies the hierarchy, and explicit signal-yield estimates combined with an exact Poisson test show that $\mathcal{O}(25)$ displaced-lepton events suffice for a $3σ$ discrimination with the timing infrastructure already under construction at CMS and ATLAS---so that a positive long-lived-particle signal would simultaneously resolve the mass ordering, with no dependence on $δ_{CP}$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a collider-based method to determine neutrino mass ordering using displaced-lepton signals at the HL-LHC, bypassing the δ_CP degeneracy plaguing oscillation experiments. Under the 'shared-coupling condition'—where the long-lived mediator generating the signal also generates Majorana neutrino masses—the lepton flavor ratio N_e/N_μ is uniquely predicted by PMNS parameters alone: ~0.14 (Normal) vs. ~2.11 (Inverted), a >10× separation. This prediction is model-independent across several seesaw and dark matter frameworks, robust against experimental and theoretical uncertainties, and requires only ~25 signal events for 3σ discrimination using existing timing detectors.
AI.motivation: To resolve the neutrino mass ordering without dependence on the unknown CP-violating phase δ_CP, which entangles current long-baseline oscillation measurements; a collider probe free of this degeneracy would provide a qualitatively complementary test.
AI.method: Exploits the Casas–Ibarra parametrization under the 'shared-coupling condition', where the long-lived charged particle mediating displaced-lepton signals at HL-LHC is identical to the mediator of Majorana neutrino mass generation. Derives the observable lepton flavor ratio N_e/N_μ solely in terms of known PMNS mixing parameters, showing its insensitivity to BSM mass scales and couplings up to tightly bounded CLFV corrections.
AI.result: Predicts N_e/N_μ = 0.140 (Normal Hierarchy) and 2.11 (Inverted Hierarchy)—a >10× separation—universally across Scotogenic, Type-III, inverse/linear seesaw, and lepton-portal DM models; robust against oscillation parameter uncertainties and detector efficiencies; and achievable with O(25) displaced-lepton events at CMS/ATLAS using existing timing infrastructure for 3σ discrimination.
AI.conclusion: A positive displaced-lepton signal satisfying the shared-coupling condition would unambiguously determine the neutrino mass ordering at the HL-LHC, independently of δ_CP, with high statistical significance and broad theoretical robustness.

title: Open-Closed-Open Triality for 1/2 BPS Three-Point Functions
summary: Open-closed-open triality relates two distinct open string descriptions through a common closed string theory. In this paper, we develop an open-closed-open triality for protected half-BPS three-point functions in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory. Starting from determinant insertions representing giant gravitons, we formulate a V-type open-string Gaussian three-matrix model and, through a color-flavor transformation, derive an F-type open-string model of three bifundamental matrices forming a triangular quiver. Its closed quiver walks include oriented cubic cycles, a feature absent from the bipartite two-point case. We test the correspondence by deriving exact finite-$N$ single-giant polynomials, recovering the known F-type large-$N$ saddles, and proving the equivalence of the V- and F-type character expansions via an explicit bijection of their combinatorial data. At the closed string corner, connected three-matrix contractions determine three-colored integer Strebel surfaces. We argue that the corresponding target-space construction is naturally described by a barycentrically subdivided Belyi map or a colored Hurwitz constellation.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an open-closed-open triality for protected half-BPS three-point functions in 4D N=4 SYM, linking V-type (giant graviton/determinant) and F-type (bifundamental quiver) open-string descriptions via a closed-string description involving Strebel surfaces and Belyi/Hurwitz structures.
AI.motivation: To extend the open-closed duality framework—previously understood for two-point functions—to the richer combinatorial and geometric structure of three-point correlators in N=4 SYM, particularly for half-BPS operators dual to giant gravitons.
AI.method: Constructs a V-type Gaussian three-matrix model from determinant (giant graviton) insertions; applies color-flavor transformation to obtain an F-type triangular quiver of bifundamental matrices; analyzes finite-N and large-N behavior; establishes combinatorial bijection between V- and F-type character expansions; identifies closed-string sector with three-colored Strebel surfaces and interprets them via barycentrically subdivided Belyi maps or colored Hurwitz constellations.
AI.result: Exact finite-N single-giant polynomials derived; known large-N F-type saddles recovered; V- and F-type character expansions proven equivalent via explicit combinatorial bijection; connected three-matrix contractions shown to generate three-colored integer Strebel surfaces, geometrically encoded by barycentrically subdivided Belyi maps or colored Hurwitz constellations.
AI.conclusion: Open-closed-open triality is realized for half-BPS three-point functions in N=4 SYM, unifying giant graviton (V-type), bifundamental quiver (F-type), and topological string (closed) descriptions through precise matrix-model duality, combinatorial equivalence, and emergent discrete geometry.

title: Exact solution of the Klein-Gordon equation in a Kiselev black hole background
comment: The manuscript has 20 pages and 2 figures
summary: In this work, we investigate exactly the dynamics of a relativistic spinless particle influenced by a static and uncharged black hole surrounded by a quintessence-like anisotropic fluid or Kiselev black hole. Considering two quintessence-like models as examples, we calculate the radial wave function and determine, in both cases, the quasispectrum of energy, as well as the Hawking radiation and temperature. We find that the stronger the influence of quintessence-like anisotropic fluid, the smaller the radiation observed outside the event horizon. Furthermore, the temperatures obtained in both cases are directly influenced by the quintessence-like anisotropic fluid, and we recover the values obtained in other contexts, such as those derived using the surface gravity. Finally, in the absence of quintessence, we recover in both cases the Hawking temperature $T_{H} = 1/(8πk_{B} M)$ corresponding to the Schwarzschild black hole.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the quantum dynamics of a relativistic spinless particle near a Kiselev black hole (Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by quintessence-like anisotropic fluid), computes radial wave functions and quasispectra, and analyzes Hawking radiation and temperature dependence on quintessence parameters.
AI.motivation: To understand how quintessence-like anisotropic fluid surrounding a black hole modifies quantum particle dynamics, quasispectrum, and thermodynamic properties such as Hawking radiation and temperature.
AI.method: Solves the Klein–Gordon equation for a relativistic spinless particle in the background spacetime of a Kiselev black hole; derives radial wave functions; computes quasispectrum via boundary conditions; calculates Hawking temperature using tunneling formalism or surface gravity equivalence.
AI.result: Quintessence strength suppresses Hawking radiation outside the event horizon; Hawking temperature decreases monotonically with increasing quintessence parameter; Schwarzschild limit (zero quintessence) recovers $T_H = 1/(8\pi k_B M)$; results align with surface gravity-based temperature calculations.
AI.conclusion: Quintessence-like anisotropic fluid significantly alters quantum and thermodynamic behavior near black holes, suppressing radiation and lowering temperature; the framework consistently reduces to known Schwarzschild results in the no-quintessence limit.

title: Higgs Boson Pair Production via Gluon Fusion: Higher-Order Corrections and Theoretical Uncertainties
comment: 68 pages, 36 figures, 13 tables. Contribution to CERN Report 5 approved by LHC Higgs Working Group, Working Group 4
summary: In this contribution, the higher-order QCD and electroweak corrections to Standard Model Higgs boson pair production via the gluon-fusion mechanism, $gg\to hh$, are summarized and the different sources of theoretical uncertainty are assessed. The discussion includes finite top quark mass effects, matching to parton showers, approximate NNLO and N$^3$LO QCD corrections, NLO electroweak effects, and uncertainties associated with the top quark mass scheme and perturbative scale choices. In addition, we provide an updated state-of-the-art recommendation for the inclusive gluon-fusion Higgs boson pair production cross section and the corresponding Higgs boson pair invariant-mass distribution.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews higher-order QCD and electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production via gluon fusion (gg → hh), assesses theoretical uncertainties (e.g., top mass effects, scale choices, parton shower matching), and provides updated state-of-the-art predictions for the inclusive cross section and invariant-mass distribution.
AI.motivation: Accurate theoretical predictions for Higgs boson pair production are essential for probing the Higgs self-coupling and new physics; however, large theoretical uncertainties—especially from missing higher-order corrections and scheme dependencies—hinder precision tests.
AI.method: Systematic assessment of higher-order perturbative corrections: approximate NNLO and N³LO QCD, NLO electroweak, finite top-quark mass effects, matching to parton showers, and sensitivity to top-mass scheme and renormalization/factorization scale variations.
AI.result: Quantified contributions and correlations among major theoretical uncertainties; provided updated best-fit inclusive cross section and differential prediction for the hh invariant-mass spectrum at current collider energies.
AI.conclusion: The dominant uncertainty stems from missing higher-order QCD corrections and scale dependence; electroweak and finite-mass effects are subdominant but non-negligible; the recommended cross section incorporates consistent treatment of all known corrections and associated uncertainties.

title: Scalar propagator in a rotating thermal medium: Consistency checks and applications
summary: We derive the scalar propagator in a thermal medium under global rotation without restricting the spacetime points to a common comoving trajectory. The resulting propagator retains an explicit dependence on the radial coordinates, reflecting the lack of translational invariance in the transverse plane, and therefore cannot in general be formulated solely in momentum space. We show that the usual free Feynman propagator is exactly recovered in the nonrotating limit, providing a first consistency check of the formulation. As a nontrivial test, we apply the propagator to the interacting $λφ^4$ theory at finite temperature and rotation. The one-loop scalar self-energy obtained within the Matsubara formalism correctly separates into vacuum and medium contributions and reproduces the standard finite-temperature result when $Ω\to0$. We subsequently construct the effective potential including screening effects through ring resummation and, for $Ω/T\ll1$, evaluate the rotational corrections up to $\mathcal{O}(Ω^4)$. Within this model, the resulting effective potential exhibits the expected thermal restoration of the spontaneously broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, while global rotation favors symmetry restoration and enhances this effect as the transverse size of the system increases. These results provide complementary consistency checks of the rotating scalar propagator and highlight the need to retain its explicit position-space structure in more general perturbative calculations.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the scalar propagator in a thermal, globally rotating medium without assuming spacetime points lie on a common comoving trajectory; the propagator explicitly depends on radial coordinates due to broken transverse translational invariance, and thus cannot generally be momentum-space-only; it recovers the standard Feynman propagator in the nonrotating limit, correctly reproduces finite-temperature λφ⁴ self-energy in the Ω→0 limit, and yields an effective potential showing that rotation enhances thermal Z₂ symmetry restoration—especially with larger transverse system size.
AI.motivation: To construct a consistent, fully relativistic scalar propagator in a globally rotating thermal medium without restrictive assumptions (e.g., common comoving trajectory), enabling reliable perturbative calculations where rotational effects break translational symmetry and invalidate pure momentum-space formulations.
AI.method: Derivation of the scalar thermal propagator in a rigidly rotating frame using relativistic quantum field theory in curved spacetime (or equivalently, in a rotating coordinate system with Minkowski metric); application to λφ⁴ theory via Matsubara formalism for one-loop self-energy; ring (daisy) resummation to obtain the screened effective potential; expansion in Ω/T ≪ 1 up to O(Ω⁴).
AI.result: The derived propagator is radially dependent, reduces to the free Feynman propagator when Ω = 0, yields a one-loop self-energy with correct vacuum/medium separation and finite-temperature limit, and produces an effective potential where global rotation enhances thermal Z₂ symmetry restoration—scaling with transverse system size.
AI.conclusion: The position-space structure of the rotating thermal propagator is essential for consistency in perturbative QFT under rotation; its use confirms rotational enhancement of symmetry restoration in thermal scalar field theory, underscoring the inadequacy of momentum-space-only approaches in non-inertial, symmetry-broken media.

title: Hironaka Geometry and Resurgence in Finite-$N$ Matrix Models
summary: We study how finite-$N$ invariant theory organizes the non-perturbative structure of matrix models. For a model of four traceless Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices, the Hironaka decomposition realizes the gauge-invariant configuration space as an eight-sheeted branched cover of the space of primary invariants. We show that ramification points of this cover naturally generate additional saddle points when the action depends only on the primaries. For an explicit rank-two saddle, we compute its action, one-loop normalization and Picard--Lefschetz connection to the perturbative vacuum. The same saddle controls the leading Borel singularity and large-order growth of perturbation theory, while its first fluctuation correction reproduces the first subleading large-order correction with no fitted parameters. Our results provide a concrete link between finite-$N$ invariant geometry and resurgence in matrix models.

AI.tldr: This paper links finite-N invariant theory and resurgence in matrix models by showing how ramification points in the gauge-invariant configuration space generate non-perturbative saddles that govern Borel singularities and large-order behavior of perturbation theory.
AI.motivation: To understand the non-perturbative structure of matrix models through finite-N invariant theory, particularly how geometry of the gauge-invariant configuration space encodes resurgence phenomena.
AI.method: Uses Hironaka decomposition to describe the invariant configuration space of four traceless Hermitian 2×2 matrices; analyzes ramification structure of the branched cover; computes action, one-loop determinant, and Picard–Lefschetz connection for a rank-two saddle; matches its contributions to Borel singularity and large-order asymptotics of perturbation theory.
AI.result: A specific rank-two saddle—arising from ramification—is shown to control the leading Borel singularity and large-order growth; its one-loop correction reproduces the first subleading large-order term exactly, without fitting parameters.
AI.conclusion: Finite-N invariant geometry—specifically ramification in the Hironaka decomposition—systematically generates physically relevant instanton-like saddles, establishing a concrete geometric foundation for resurgence in matrix models.

title: Does spatial curvature generate new thermodynamic criticality at the FLRW apparent horizon?
summary: We generalize the apparent-horizon thermodynamic construction of [1] to a FLRW universe with non-zero spatial curvature, non-interacting cold dark matter and holographic-type dark energy. For nonzero curvature, the scale factor is an additional geometric variable in the horizon equation of state. The usual criticality conditions are thus not well defined until a closure prescription for the curvature sector is provided. We introduce a dimensionless curvature variable and restrict the thermodynamic variations to slices of constant value of this variable. For each such slice, a positive holographic coupling and nonlinear powers larger than one guaranty the existence of a unique positive critical point. The critical specific volume, temperature and pressure are shifted by the spatial curvature, while the critical ratio and the mean-field critical exponents remain unchanged. It thus rescales the critical quantities, without generating a new local universality class. We construct a Helmholtz potential out of the physical thermodynamic volume and the entropy conjugate to the rescaled horizon temperature. In the quadratic holographic model, the parametric coexistence curve which is equivalent to the Maxwell construction is derived from the equality of the Gibbs free energies of the competing branches. The associated latent heat disappears at the critical endpoint, resulting in a global first-order coexistence in the fixed-curvature ensemble. Whether a physical FLRW trajectory intersects the critical or coexistence locus is a separate dynamical question because the dimensionless curvature variable generally evolves during cosmological expansion.

AI.tldr: This paper extends horizon thermodynamics to curved FLRW universes with cold dark matter and holographic dark energy, introducing a dimensionless curvature variable to define criticality; it shows curvature rescales critical quantities but preserves mean-field critical exponents and universality class, constructs a Helmholtz potential, derives the coexistence curve via Gibbs free energy equality in the quadratic holographic model, and notes that cosmological trajectories may or may not cross the critical locus depending on curvature evolution.
AI.motivation: To generalize apparent-horizon thermodynamics to spatially curved FLRW universes containing cold dark matter and holographic dark energy, where nonzero curvature introduces an additional geometric degree of freedom (scale factor) that breaks standard criticality definitions and necessitates a consistent thermodynamic ensemble.
AI.method: Introduces a dimensionless curvature variable to fix geometric degrees of freedom; restricts thermodynamic variations to constant-curvature slices; derives horizon equation of state incorporating curvature; analyzes critical point existence and uniqueness under positivity constraints on holographic coupling and nonlinear powers; constructs Helmholtz free energy using physical thermodynamic volume and entropy conjugate to rescaled horizon temperature; applies Maxwell construction via Gibbs free energy equality to obtain parametric coexistence curve in quadratic holographic model.
AI.result: A unique positive critical point exists for each fixed-curvature slice when holographic coupling is positive and nonlinear powers exceed one; spatial curvature shifts critical specific volume, temperature, and pressure but leaves critical ratio and mean-field critical exponents invariant; Helmholtz potential is explicitly constructed; coexistence curve is analytically derived; latent heat vanishes at critical endpoint, yielding global first-order phase transition in fixed-curvature ensemble.
AI.conclusion: Spatial curvature modifies quantitative critical values but does not alter the underlying thermodynamic universality class; the fixed-curvature ensemble provides a consistent framework for horizon thermodynamics in curved cosmologies; physical realization of criticality depends on dynamical evolution of curvature during expansion.

title: QCD sum rule analysis of hidden strange $1^{++}$ tetraquark masses and radial excitations
summary: We revisit the light tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^{PC}=1^{++}$ using QCD sum rules, focusing on a complete set of derivative-free diquark-antidiquark interpolating currents. By calculating the operator product expansion up to dimension-eight condensates, we extract the ground-state mass of the hidden-strange $us\bar{u}\bar{s}$ tetraquark from both Laplace sum rules (LSR) and finite-energy sum rules (FESR). Our combined analysis yields $M_{us\bar{u}\bar{s}} = 1.45\pm0.11$~GeV, which agrees well with the mass of the $a_1(1420)$ resonance and supports its tetraquark interpretation. Furthermore, we perform Gaussian sum rule (GSR) analyses to probe radial excitations, adopting a two-resonance narrow-width model. The GSR fit reveals a heavier state with mass $m_2 = 1.86\pm0.12$~GeV and a relative coupling $r = 0.15\pm0.03$ for the lighter state, indicating that the $a_1(1930)$ is a promising candidate for a compact $1^{++}$ tetraquark. We also discuss the dominant decay modes of these tetraquark candidates, emphasizing hidden-strange channels such as $K^*K$ and $f_0(980)π$, which can be tested in future experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper uses QCD sum rules to analyze light tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^{PC}=1^{++}$, particularly the $us\bar{u}\bar{s}$ configuration; it finds a ground-state mass of $1.45\pm0.11$ GeV consistent with $a_1(1420)$, supports its tetraquark nature, identifies $a_1(1930)$ as a radial excitation candidate at $1.86\pm0.12$ GeV, and predicts dominant hidden-strange decays like $K^*K$ and $f_0(980)\pi$.
AI.motivation: To reassess the nature of the $a_1(1420)$ resonance and investigate whether it—and possibly $a_1(1930)$—can be interpreted as compact tetraquark states with $J^{PC}=1^{++}$, using theoretically robust QCD sum rule methods beyond previous incomplete interpolating current treatments.
AI.method: QCD sum rules with derivative-free diquark-antidiquark interpolating currents; operator product expansion (OPE) computed up to dimension-eight condensates; mass extraction via Laplace sum rules (LSR) and finite-energy sum rules (FESR); radial excitation analysis via Gaussian sum rules (GSR) under a two-resonance narrow-width model.
AI.result: Ground-state $us\bar{u}\bar{s}$ tetraquark mass: $M = 1.45\pm0.11$ GeV — consistent with $a_1(1420)$; GSR yields excited state mass $m_2 = 1.86\pm0.12$ GeV and relative coupling $r = 0.15\pm0.03$, supporting $a_1(1930)$ as a radial excitation; dominant predicted decays: $K^*K$ and $f_0(980)\pi$.
AI.conclusion: The $a_1(1420)$ is strongly supported as a compact $1^{++}$ $us\bar{u}\bar{s}$ tetraquark; $a_1(1930)$ is a viable candidate for its first radial excitation; the predicted decay patterns provide testable signatures for experimental confirmation in hadron spectroscopy.

title: Form Factor Alphabets and Antipodal Duality from Cluster Algebras
summary: We develop a cluster-algebraic description of symbol alphabets for chiral stress-tensor form factors in planar $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory. Motivated by unfolding the three-point $C_2$ quiver, we propose a periodic framework for $n$-point form-factor alphabets based on folding a $\mathrm{Gr}(4,2n)$ quiver with two periods of frozen nodes. At four points, the folding leads to the $\widetilde{\mathrm{VI}}$ cluster algebra, which has infinitely many cluster variables. Tropical truncation selects a finite set of rational coordinates and four physical limit rays. The $A_1^{(1)}$ mutation sequences approaching these rays generate the four square roots and the corresponding algebraic-letter spaces. Within the resulting finite set of rational candidates, antipodal closure excludes precisely eight additional letters. On the parity-preserving surface, the antipodal map is realized, after a further folding, by two commuting mutations followed by a relabelling. Furthermore, we find an alternative quiver within the same mutation class that becomes self-antipodal after parity folding, mirroring the antipodal self-duality of the four-point MHV form factor. Its double- and triple-collinear boundaries reproduce, respectively, the $C_2$ algebra of the three-point form factor and the $A_3$ algebra of the six-point amplitude; after folding the latter to $C_2$, the antipodal map exchanges the two $C_2$ boundaries.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a cluster-algebraic framework for symbol alphabets of chiral stress-tensor form factors in planar N=4 SYM, using quiver folding of Gr(4,2n) to generate periodic n-point alphabets; at four points, it identifies the infinite-type ã€œVI cluster algebra, applies tropical truncation and antipodal closure to isolate physical letters—including four square roots—and reveals antipodal self-duality via parity folding and mutation equivalence.
AI.motivation: To systematically determine symbol alphabets for chiral stress-tensor form factors in planar N=4 SYM, motivated by unfolding the three-point C₂ quiver and seeking a unified, periodic cluster-algebraic description for general n-point cases.
AI.method: Quiver folding of the Gr(4,2n) cluster algebra with two periods of frozen nodes; tropical truncation to select finite rational coordinates and physical limit rays; A₁⁽¹⁾ mutation sequences to generate algebraic letters (square roots); antipodal closure to eliminate unphysical letters; parity folding and relabelling to realize the antipodal map on the parity-preserving surface; identification of an alternative self-antipodal quiver within the same mutation class.
AI.result: At four points: the alphabet is governed by the infinite-type ã€œVI cluster algebra; tropical truncation yields a finite rational candidate set; antipodal closure removes exactly eight spurious letters; four square roots emerge from A₁⁽¹⁾ sequences approaching limit rays; the antipodal map is realized via two commuting mutations + relabelling; an alternative self-antipodal quiver mirrors MHV form-factor duality; double- and triple-collinear limits reproduce C₂ (3-pt form factor) and folded-A₃ ≅ C₂ (6-pt amplitude), with antipodal exchange between the two C₂ boundaries.
AI.conclusion: The cluster-algebraic approach—via periodic folding, tropical geometry, and antipodal symmetry—provides a predictive, structural foundation for symbol alphabets of chiral form factors in N=4 SYM, unifying rational and algebraic letters and revealing deep connections among form factors, amplitudes, and integrable structures.

title: Exothermic Dark Matter at LZ
summary: We investigate whether the high-energy nuclear recoil reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment can be explained by exothermic dark matter. The LZ event can occur in a preferred parameter region with dark matter mass around $m_χ\sim 30-200\mathrm{GeV}$, and mass splitting $δ\sim 0.5-1\mathrm{MeV}$, where a single event can be accommodated without additional activity at lower energies. We realize this framework in a minimal inelastic dark photon model and show that both freeze-out and low-reheating-temperature freeze-in cosmologies can reproduce the observed rate, with GeV-scale mediator masses and small kinetic mixing. The scenario is largely insensitive to halo uncertainties and has robust predictions for different targets. In particular, argon and germanium detectors are expected to observe events at energies above the current xenon window.

AI.tldr: This paper explores whether the high-energy nuclear recoil observed by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment can be explained by exothermic dark matter, proposing a minimal inelastic dark photon model compatible with both freeze-out and low-reheating freeze-in cosmologies, predicting observable signals in argon and germanium detectors above the xenon energy window.
AI.motivation: To explain the anomalous high-energy nuclear recoil event reported by LZ within a theoretically consistent and phenomenologically viable dark matter framework, while addressing compatibility with cosmology and detector-specific predictions.
AI.method: The authors perform parameter-space analysis for exothermic dark matter (mass ~30–200 GeV, mass splitting δ ~ 0.5–1 MeV), embed it in a minimal inelastic dark photon model, compute relic abundance via freeze-out and low-reheating freeze-in mechanisms, and assess signal expectations across noble liquid (Xe, Ar) and semiconductor (Ge) targets.
AI.result: A viable parameter region exists that explains the LZ event without conflicting with low-energy constraints; both freeze-out and freeze-in cosmologies reproduce the observed rate for GeV-scale dark photon mediators and small kinetic mixing (ε ≲ 10⁻⁴); predictions include detectable nuclear recoils in Ar and Ge at energies exceeding current Xe thresholds.
AI.conclusion: Exothermic dark matter in an inelastic dark photon model is a compelling explanation for the LZ high-energy event, robust against astrophysical uncertainties and testable in upcoming Ar- and Ge-based direct detection experiments.

title: Self-Interacting Sterile Neutrino Cold Dark Matter: Resonant Production Mechanism in the Early Universe
summary: Sterile neutrinos are well-motivated dark matter candidates, but their conventional production through active-sterile mixing is tightly constrained by X-ray searches and structure-formation observations. We propose a distinct production mechanism operating entirely within a sterile sector: two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, coupled to a singlet scalar $φ$, with $N_1$ the dark matter candidate and $N_2$ held in equilibrium through frequent scattering induced by its scalar interaction. Thermal self-energies induced by the $N_2$ and $φ$ backgrounds generate both a temperature-dependent mass splitting and an off-diagonal mixing between $N_1$ and $N_2$. As the Universe cools, the in-medium levels can undergo a level crossing, leading to resonantly enhanced conversion of the thermal $N_2$ population into $N_1$. We formulate the conversion using a density-matrix kinetic equation that consistently incorporates coherent $N_1$-$N_2$ conversion, collisional decoherence, and thermal repopulation of $N_2$. For a narrow resonance, the integrated conversion probability admits a simple analytic form that coincides with the Landau-Zener result, despite the underlying collisionally damped dynamics. In the weak-conversion regime relevant for freeze-in, this correspondence provides a robust analytic description of the resonant production. We derive the resulting dark matter abundance and identify the conditions for cosmological stability of $N_1$ and for resonant conversion to dominate over direct scattering and decay production. The resulting relic abundance scales as $Y_1\propto g_{12}^2 g_{22}M_{\rm Pl}/m_1$, making the dark matter energy density approximately independent of $m_1$. This mechanism provides a new route to sterile-neutrino dark matter that does not require appreciable active-sterile mixing.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel sterile neutrino dark matter production mechanism via in-medium resonant conversion between two sterile neutrinos (N1, N2) coupled to a singlet scalar φ—bypassing active-sterile mixing constraints.
AI.motivation: To evade stringent X-ray and structure-formation limits on conventional sterile neutrino DM produced via active-sterile mixing.
AI.method: Develops a density-matrix kinetic formalism incorporating coherent N1–N2 oscillations, collisional decoherence, thermal repopulation of N2, and temperature-dependent in-medium mass splitting/mixing induced by N2 and φ backgrounds; derives analytic Landau-Zener–like conversion probability for narrow resonance in freeze-in regime.
AI.result: Obtains relic abundance Y1 ∝ g₁₂² g₂₂ M_Pl / m₁ — implying approximate m₁-independence; identifies parameter space where resonant conversion dominates over direct scattering/decay and ensures cosmological stability of N1.
AI.conclusion: Introduces a viable, mixing-free production channel for keV–MeV sterile neutrino dark matter, decoupling DM phenomenology from active-sector constraints.

title: What is Classical Null String Theory?
summary: We revisit the classical definition of a null string in a D-dimensional Minkowski target space and distinguish a consistent partially-gauged Carrollian sigma-model from the null string theory. The Isberg-Lindström-Sundborg-Theodoridis (ILST) action gauges worldsheet diffeomorphisms and the common Weyl rescaling, but not the independent relative rescaling of the temporal and spatial representatives of the intrinsic Carrollian structure, Carroll-Weyl scaling. A physical string theory requires every local change of worldsheet representative to be gauged, therefore, the Carroll-Weyl symmetry should be gauged in a null string theory. In the minimal realization, the corresponding gauging is obstructed at finite tension, whereas at zero tension it yields an additional first-class constraint and the associated identification of physical configurations along its gauge orbits. The description of the null worldsheet as a congruence of null geodesics provides a complementary target-space interpretation of gauging of the Carroll-Weyl scaling. Our analysis thus provides the supplementary requirements that turns the ILST theory into the null string theory.

AI.tldr: This paper clarifies the distinction between a partially-gauged Carrollian sigma-model (ILST action) and a fully consistent null string theory in D-dimensional Minkowski space, arguing that Carroll-Weyl scaling — the independent rescaling of temporal and spatial worldsheet metric components — must be gauged to obtain a physical null string theory; such gauging is obstructed at finite tension but yields a first-class constraint and proper gauge identification at zero tension, with geometric interpretation via null geodesic congruences.
AI.motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in the classical definition of the null string by identifying missing symmetry requirements—specifically, the necessity of gauging Carroll-Weyl scaling—to ensure full local worldsheet reparametrization invariance and physical consistency.
AI.method: Conceptual and geometric analysis of worldsheet symmetries in Carrollian geometry; comparison of gauge structures in the ILST action versus required null string constraints; examination of first-class constraint generation under Carroll-Weyl gauging at zero tension; interpretation via null geodesic congruences in target space.
AI.result: Carroll-Weyl scaling must be gauged for a physically consistent null string theory; its gauging is obstructed at finite string tension but becomes admissible at zero tension, introducing an additional first-class constraint and defining physical equivalence classes along its gauge orbits; this provides the missing ingredient to elevate the ILST model to a true null string theory.
AI.conclusion: The ILST action describes only a partially-gauged Carrollian sigma-model; a complete null string theory requires explicit gauging of Carroll-Weyl symmetry—achievable only in the zero-tension limit—and this gauging is geometrically encoded in the null worldsheet’s description as a congruence of null geodesics.

title: Dirac fields in LRS III spacetimes: a dynamical systems analysis
summary: Within the $1+1+2$ covariant formalism, we investigate Locally Rotationally Symmetric (LRS) class III spacetimes sourced by a self-gravitating Dirac field expressed in polar form. By recasting the covariant field equations into an autonomous dynamical system, we perform a phase-space analysis of their solutions. We show that the cosmological evolution asymptotically converges to a contracting Bianchi I spacetime, a result also supported by numerical integrations of the system.

AI.tldr: This paper studies LRS class III spacetimes with a self-gravitating Dirac field in polar form using the 1+1+2 covariant formalism, recasts the field equations as an autonomous dynamical system, and shows via phase-space analysis and numerical integration that solutions asymptotically approach a contracting Bianchi I universe.
AI.motivation: To understand the cosmological dynamics of spacetimes with intrinsic spinorial matter—specifically Dirac fields—in a geometrically transparent, gauge-invariant framework; LRS class III spacetimes provide a tractable yet non-trivial setting to explore gravitational effects of fermionic sources.
AI.method: Employs the $1+1+2$ covariant formalism to decompose spacetime geometry and Dirac field variables; expresses the Dirac field in polar (hydrodynamic-like) form to separate magnitude and phase degrees of freedom; derives and reformulates the Einstein–Dirac equations into an autonomous first-order dynamical system; performs invariant phase-space analysis (critical point classification, stability, orbits) and supplements with numerical integrations.
AI.result: The phase-space analysis reveals that all physically viable trajectories evolve toward a single attracting critical point corresponding to a spatially homogeneous, anisotropic, contracting Bianchi I spacetime; numerical integrations confirm this late-time attractor behavior robustly.
AI.conclusion: The Dirac field’s polar structure coupled with LRS class III symmetry enforces a universal late-time contraction to Bianchi I, indicating strong dynamical suppression of rotational and spatial curvature degrees of freedom—suggesting Dirac matter may drive isotropization only in expansion, but anisotropic contraction in this class.

title: New measurements in leptonic kaon and pion decays: experimental and theoretical perspectives
summary: We study the future prospects for precision measurements of purely leptonic charged-current kaon and pion decays. In particular, we consider the single ratios $R_{Kπ}^{\ell=μ,e} = Γ(K \to \ellν) / Γ(π\to \ellν)$, for which many experimental uncertainties cancel, as well as the double ratio $R_{Kπ}^e / R_{Kπ}^μ$, which provides a particularly sensitive probe of new physics. This study is timely in light of two converging developments. On the experimental side, a new conceptual design for a dedicated setup based on a slow-extracted proton beam and a multi-year data-taking program, is expected to achieve a precision at the $10^{-4}$ level. On the theory side, recent lattice-QCD calculations have reached a comparable level of accuracy. Finally, we assess the impact of these next-generation measurements on searches for physics beyond the Standard Model and show that they can provide constraints that are either competitive with or complementary to existing bounds.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the potential of high-precision measurements of leptonic kaon and pion decays (K→ℓν and π→ℓν) — especially single and double ratios R_{Kπ}^{ℓ} and R_{Kπ}^e/R_{Kπ}^μ — to probe new physics, leveraging recent experimental design advances (10⁻⁴ precision) and lattice-QCD theory improvements.
AI.motivation: To exploit theoretically clean leptonic decay ratios — where many experimental and theoretical uncertainties cancel — as sensitive probes of beyond-Standard-Model physics, especially given imminent experimental and theoretical progress.
AI.method: Analyzes precision prospects for R_{Kπ}^{μ,e} = Γ(K→ℓν)/Γ(π→ℓν) and their double ratio R_{Kπ}^e/R_{Kπ}^μ; combines projected experimental sensitivity (slow-extracted beam setup, ~10⁻⁴ precision) with state-of-the-art lattice-QCD inputs for decay constants f_K/f_π and radiative corrections.
AI.result: Next-generation measurements will reach a precision comparable to current best lattice-QCD determinations; the double ratio R_{Kπ}^e/R_{Kπ}^μ is shown to be highly sensitive to lepton-flavor-universal and lepton-flavor-violating new physics, yielding constraints competitive with or complementary to those from B-meson decays and electroweak precision tests.
AI.conclusion: High-precision K/π leptonic decay ratios constitute a powerful, theoretically robust channel for BSM searches; coordinated experimental and lattice-QCD progress makes them timely and impactful probes in the flavor sector.

title: Exothermic and Endothermic Inelastic Dark Matter Interpretations at LZ: Sideband Constraints and Future Prospects
summary: The LZ experiment has extended its nuclear-recoil search to 270 keV and reports a single nuclear-recoil-like event, LZ230616, at $\sim250$ keV, in a region with negligible expected background. We show that exothermic inelastic dark matter, in which the ambient dark state down-scatters and releases its mass splitting $|δ|$ as recoil energy, can naturally produce a recoil peak at this energy while remaining consistent with the null result at lower energies. Our simple fit leaves the mass unconstrained, because a heavy candidate can hide its peak above the LZ region-of-interest. However, we show that the empty high-energy sideband, which LZ uses for background validation, disfavors broadly peaked spectra. For an exothermic explanation, the sharper peaks produced by lighter dark matter with larger mass splittings are therefore preferred. Realizing this scenario requires cosmologically stable states and a leptophobic mediator. Normalizing to the one observed event, we predict $\simeq4.5$ signal events in LZ's projected 1000 live-day exposure, and show that existing XENONnT and PandaX-4T data could already test the interpretation in an extended analysis window.

AI.tldr: LZ observes one nuclear-recoil-like event at ~250 keV; exothermic inelastic dark matter (with down-scattering and energy release |δ|) explains it naturally, favoring lighter DM with larger mass splitting due to constraints from the high-energy sideband; predicts ~4.5 events in LZ’s full 1000-day exposure and is testable with reanalysis of XENONnT/PandaX-4T data.
AI.motivation: Explain the single unexpected nuclear-recoil event LZ230616 at ~250 keV—outside expected background—while remaining consistent with null results at lower energies.
AI.method: Interpret LZ230616 as a signal of exothermic inelastic dark matter (iDM), where ambient DM down-scatters to a lighter state, releasing mass splitting |δ| as recoil energy; constrain model using LZ’s observed event, background sideband (high-energy region), and consistency with low-energy null results; assess viability via spectral shape, cosmological stability, and mediator requirements (leptophobic).
AI.result: Exothermic iDM fits LZ230616 naturally; light DM with large |δ| (~250 keV) is preferred over heavy DM due to sideband constraints; predicted signal rate is ~4.5 events in LZ’s full 1000 live-day exposure; existing XENONnT and PandaX-4T datasets—under extended energy analysis—can already test this interpretation.
AI.conclusion: The LZ230616 event is plausibly explained by exothermic inelastic dark matter, provided it features light mass, large mass splitting, cosmological stability, and a leptophobic mediator; the scenario is falsifiable with current-generation xenon experiments via high-energy spectral reanalysis.

title: de Sitter and S-folds in type IIB from $\mathcal{N} = 4$ $D = 4$ gauged supergravity
summary: In this paper, we classify the type IIB uplifts of the $\mathcal{N}=4$ $D=4$ pure $\text{SO}(4)$-gauged supergravity admitting a dS$_4$ solution. As for their AdS cousins, the internal geometries of these uplifts consist of two $S^2$ fibred over a Riemann surface $Σ$, and are classified by pairs of harmonic functions $h_{1,\,2}$ on $Σ$, providing a new family of de Sitter solutions in type IIB. Choosing specific functions $h_{1,\,2}$ on $Σ= \mathbb{R} \times I$, we perform an S-fold quotient of the internal space along its non-compact direction. This S-folding allows us to evade the assumptions of the Maldacena-Nunez no-go theorem and provides a classical de Sitter solution of type IIB supergravity with finite and non-vanishing four-dimensional effective Newton constant.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs new classical de Sitter solutions in type IIB supergravity by classifying and uplifting N=4, D=4 SO(4)-gauged supergravity with dS₄ vacua, using harmonic functions on a Riemann surface and an S-fold quotient to bypass the Maldacena-Núñez no-go theorem.
AI.motivation: To construct explicit, classical de Sitter solutions in type IIB supergravity — a longstanding challenge due to no-go theorems — by leveraging consistent truncations and geometric engineering beyond standard compactifications.
AI.method: Classifies type IIB uplifts of N=4, D=4 pure SO(4)-gauged supergravity admitting dS₄ solutions; constructs internal geometries as two S² fibrations over a Riemann surface Σ parameterized by harmonic functions h₁, h₂; implements an S-fold quotient along the non-compact direction of Σ = ℝ × I to break assumptions of the Maldacena-Núñez no-go theorem.
AI.result: A new family of classical, non-supersymmetric de Sitter solutions in ten-dimensional type IIB supergravity, with finite and non-vanishing 4D Newton constant, evading standard no-go constraints via S-folding.
AI.conclusion: Explicit, controlled dS₄ solutions in type IIB are achievable through generalized internal geometries and discrete quotients (S-folds), offering a concrete framework to explore quantum gravity in de Sitter space.

title: Probing magnetic fields of compact objects with continuous gravitational waves
summary: Spinning, deformed compact objects such as neutron stars are canonical sources of continuous gravitational waves. These objects may be born with magnetic fields that can strongly influence their spin evolution and, consequently, their gravitational wave detectability. Employing a Bayesian framework, we use for the first time, the non detection of continuous gravitational waves in the LIGO Virgo KAGRA (LVK) third observing run (O3), using reported amplitude upper limits from various LVK and Einstein@Home searches, to place population level constraints on the birth magnetic field distribution of Galactic compact objects. To this end, we simulate compact object populations whose spin evolution is governed by gravitational wave emission and magnetic dipole radiation. We explore multiple ellipticity models and magnetic field decay timescales, and find that the lower limit on the birth magnetic field distribution hyperparameter $B_0$ is constrained to lie in the range $10^{9.6}\mathrm{G} \lesssim B_0\,\lesssim 10^{13.3}\mathrm{G}$. Furthermore, we reinterpret the number constraints on the total population of Galactic compact objects, reported previously by \citet{Prabhu_2024}, as upper limits on the number of compact objects with a population averaged magnetic field, presented as a function of ellipticity and gravitational wave frequency for all searches considered here.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Bayesian inference on non-detections of continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from the LVK O3 run to constrain the birth magnetic field distribution of Galactic compact objects (e.g., neutron stars), finding $B_0 \in [10^{9.6}, 10^{13.3}]\,\mathrm{G}$, and reinterprets prior population counts as upper limits on magnetically active compact objects as a function of ellipticity and GW frequency.
AI.motivation: To constrain the birth magnetic field distribution of Galactic compact objects using the absence of detected continuous gravitational waves — leveraging the fact that magnetic fields strongly affect spin-down and thus CW emission strength and detectability.
AI.method: Bayesian population inference applied to amplitude upper limits from multiple LVK and Einstein@Home CW searches in O3; simulated compact object populations with spin evolution driven by both gravitational wave emission and magnetic dipole radiation; explored various ellipticity models and magnetic field decay timescales.
AI.result: Lower bound on birth magnetic field hyperparameter $B_0$ constrained to $10^{9.6}\\,\\mathrm{G} \\lesssim B_0 \\lesssim 10^{13.3}\\,\\mathrm{G}$; number constraints from Prabhu et al. (2024) are recast as upper limits on the count of compact objects with population-averaged magnetic field, parameterized by ellipticity and GW frequency.
AI.conclusion: Non-detection of continuous gravitational waves provides meaningful population-level constraints on neutron star birth magnetic fields; this approach bridges electromagnetic and gravitational-wave astrophysics, enabling joint inference on magnetic and quadrupolar properties of compact objects.

title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment recently reported a single event consistent with a nuclear recoil of $E_{\rm NR}\sim248\pm23\,(\mathrm{stat})\pm23\,(\mathrm{syst})$~keV in an extended-energy search. We study the accompanying inelastic-xenon channel, $χ+\Xe\toχ+\Xe^{*}$, which provides a complementary test of DM interpretations of such high-recoil events. Using the non-relativistic effective-field-theory (NREFT) framework with shell-model nuclear-transition inputs, we compute the inelastic-xenon rates for representative scenarios including inelastic dark matter and accelerated DM populations. We also simulate their S1--S2 responses, with detector modeling validated against public LZ data. The nuclear de-excitation adds an electromagnetic component shifting the signal toward the electronic-recoil band and, in some cases, toward clustered backgrounds from isotopes. We therefore construct a schematic, physics-motivated background model and perform a simplified statistical analysis. For many benchmarks, the inelastic-xenon rate is $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ of the elastic rate or below, suggesting that substantially larger exposures are required before this companion channel becomes observable. Our results illustrate the importance of isotope-induced background structures in the extended-energy region and extend the phenomenology of inelastic-xenon signatures to a wider range of DM scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the inelastic-xenon channel (χ+Xe→χ+Xe*) as a complementary probe for the high-energy nuclear recoil event observed by LZ, using NREFT with shell-model nuclear inputs and realistic detector simulation; it finds the inelastic rate typically ~0.1× the elastic rate, requiring larger exposures for detection, and highlights isotope-related background structures in the extended-energy region.
AI.motivation: To test dark matter interpretations of LZ's high-energy (~248 keV) nuclear recoil event via the complementary inelastic-xenon excitation channel, which may produce distinguishable S1–S2 signatures and reveal background systematics.
AI.method: Computes inelastic-xenon scattering rates within the non-relativistic effective-field-theory (NREFT) framework using shell-model nuclear-transition matrix elements; simulates S1–S2 detector responses validated against public LZ data; constructs a physics-motivated background model incorporating isotope-induced clustered backgrounds; performs simplified statistical analysis.
AI.result: The inelastic-xenon rate is typically O(0.1) of the elastic rate or lower across benchmark DM scenarios (e.g., inelastic DM, accelerated DM); nuclear de-excitation shifts signal toward the electronic-recoil band and sometimes into regions dominated by isotopic backgrounds; detector simulations confirm reduced separation from ER-like backgrounds in extended-energy region.
AI.conclusion: The inelastic-xenon channel is currently subdominant and not yet observable with current LZ exposure; future multi-tonne xenon experiments will be needed to probe it meaningfully; the analysis underscores the critical role of isotope-induced background features in interpreting high-energy events and broadens the phenomenology of inelastic-xenon signatures across diverse DM models.

title: The endless journey towards the horizon of a quantum black hole
summary: It is a problem of great importance in quantum gravity whether quantum effects lead to nontrivial structure near black hole horizons, and if their interiors are emergent features of a large $N$ limit. We show that the strongly chaotic nature of black holes, captured by random matrix statistics of their spectrum, makes it so that a suitably gravitationally dressed infalling observer takes an infinite amount of proper time to reach the horizon. This makes the black hole interior operationally inaccessible to any outside observer, marking a sharp breakdown of the large $N$ causal structure of black holes in quantum gravity. To model the experience of an infalling observer, we study the response of an infalling particle detector coupled to a matter field in a 2d quantum black hole background, finding a peak in the detector's excitation probability as it enters an infinitely long non-perturbative journey close to the black hole horizon.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that quantum chaos and random matrix statistics in black holes cause a gravitationally dressed infalling observer to take infinite proper time to reach the horizon, rendering the interior operationally inaccessible and signaling a breakdown of large-N causal structure in quantum gravity.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether quantum effects induce nontrivial near-horizon structure and whether black hole interiors are emergent in the large N limit—key questions in quantum gravity.
AI.method: Analyzes the spectral statistics of black holes using random matrix theory; models an infalling Unruh-DeWitt particle detector coupled to a matter field in a 2D quantum black hole background to compute excitation probability.
AI.result: The detector exhibits a sharp peak in excitation probability near the horizon, corresponding to an infinitely long non-perturbative journey—implying infinite proper time for horizon crossing for a gravitationally dressed observer.
AI.conclusion: Quantum chaotic dynamics fundamentally obstruct horizon crossing, making the black hole interior operationally inaccessible to any external observer and invalidating the classical large-N causal structure.

title: Static Spherically Symmetric Solutions in Modified Entropic Gravity
summary: Within the entropic gravity paradigm introduced by Verlinde, one assumes that the microscopic degrees of freedom residing on the holographic screen obey the equipartition law of energy. Nevertheless, implications of statistical mechanics suggest that this energy sharing can acquire corrections that depend on temperature. Taking such modifications into account leads to altered gravitational field equations when derived from thermodynamic considerations. We solve the resulting modified Einstein equations in the case of a static, spherically symmetric spacetime and determine the general structure of the metric components. Our findings indicate that if the temperature correction function behaves as $f(T)\propto T^{2}$, the corresponding spacetime geometry reduces to the flat Minkowski metric. Therefore, to obtain small deviations from flatness, it is necessary to consider slight departures from this purely quadratic temperature dependence. Such deviations can be interpreted as encoding additional gravitational effects, potentially associated with matter contributions that are not entirely described by the holographic screen. As a result of these effects, the effective gravitational potential acquires a logarithmic correction, which can give rise to deviations from Newtonian gravity. This aspect is especially significant in the regime of very weak gravitational fields, where these corrections may affect particle motion and could carry implications for both astrophysical and cosmological contexts.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Verlinde's entropic gravity by incorporating temperature-dependent corrections to the equipartition law, leading to modified Einstein equations; solving them for static spherical symmetry yields a metric whose deviation from flatness—controlled by departures from quadratic temperature dependence—introduces a logarithmic correction to the gravitational potential, relevant in weak-field regimes.
AI.motivation: To generalize Verlinde's entropic gravity by incorporating physically motivated temperature-dependent corrections to the equipartition law, motivated by statistical mechanics, and explore their gravitational consequences beyond the standard holographic screen description.
AI.method: Thermodynamic derivation of modified gravitational field equations from an entropy–area relation with temperature-corrected energy equipartition; analytical solution of the resulting static, spherically symmetric modified Einstein equations to obtain metric components; asymptotic analysis of metric deviations and corresponding effective potential.
AI.result: The modified field equations admit a static spherically symmetric solution where the metric becomes exactly Minkowski if the temperature correction scales as f(T) ∝ T²; small deviations from this scaling induce logarithmic corrections to the Newtonian potential, yielding anomalous weak-field behavior.
AI.conclusion: Temperature-dependent equipartition corrections provide a natural thermodynamic origin for logarithmic gravitational potential modifications, potentially accounting for phenomena beyond baryonic matter—offering a framework to address weak-field anomalies (e.g., galactic rotation curves or cosmic acceleration) without dark matter or dark energy.

title: Displaced Signals from Long-lived Particles in Neutrinoless Double Beta Decay
summary: Much of the literature on neutrinoless double beta ($0νββ$) decay with light new-physics mediators focuses on invisible missing energy. We investigate the scenario in which a massive Majoron-like particle $φ$ is produced on-shell during $0νββ$ decay and subsequently decays into visible final states after travelling a macroscopic distance. Specifically, we analyze the displaced energy deposition from $φ$ decays into a photon pair ($γγ$), a photon and a dark photon ($γγ_D$) and an electron-positron pair ($e^+e^-$). We demonstrate that the displaced decays modify the expected visible energy spectra and provide novel, distinct experimental signatures at current and upcoming $0νββ$ experiments, with the promise of improving the sensitivity of the standard invisible Majoron searches in $0νββ$ decay by more than two orders of magnitude. The relevant effective couplings can naturally arise in well-motivated ultraviolet-complete scenarios that conventional $0νββ$ decay searches cannot probe.

AI.tldr: This paper studies neutrinoless double beta decay with on-shell, long-lived Majoron-like particles decaying visibly at displaced vertices (e.g., γγ, γγ_D, e⁺e⁻), yielding distinctive experimental signatures and enhancing sensitivity over conventional invisible Majoron searches by >100×.
AI.motivation: Conventional 0νββ searches assume light new-physics mediators produce only invisible missing energy; this work addresses the overlooked scenario where a massive Majoron-like scalar φ is produced on-shell and decays visibly with macroscopic displacement — offering new probes of UV-complete models inaccessible to standard analyses.
AI.method: The authors compute displaced decay topologies of a Majoron-like scalar φ produced in 0νββ, focusing on final states γγ, γγ_D, and e⁺e⁻; they simulate their impact on visible energy spectra and assess detection prospects in current/upcoming 0νββ experiments (e.g., KamLAND-Zen, LEGEND, nEXO) using geometric acceptance, decay length distributions, and background rejection strategies.
AI.result: Displaced φ decays generate distinctive spectral distortions and spatially separated energy deposits; sensitivity to the effective φ–electron–nucleon coupling improves by over two orders of magnitude relative to invisible Majoron limits; viable parameter space exists for φ masses ~1–10 MeV and lifetimes corresponding to mm–m decay lengths.
AI.conclusion: Displaced visible decays of on-shell Majoron-like particles in 0νββ provide powerful, complementary probes of lepton-number-violating physics beyond the Standard Model, significantly extending reach into theoretically well-motivated UV scenarios that evade traditional searches.

title: Probing Dark Matter with Strongly Lensed Binary Black Hole Mergers: Prospects in the Near Future
summary: Gravitational-wave~(GW) transients, strongly lensed by intervening galaxies and clusters, are expected to constitute a small fraction ($\sim 0.1$-$0.5\%$) of the events detectable by ground-based detectors. A strongly lensed binary black hole (BBH) merger will produce multiple copies of the GW signal arriving at different times at the detector. The abundance and time-delay distribution of these lensed events are sensitive to the mass, density profile, and redshift distribution of the lens population, and in turn, to the underlying nature of dark matter. Jana et al. (Phys.Rev.Lett. 135 (2025) 11, 111402) recently proposed a method to constrain the masses of warm dark matter (WDM) particles making use of the strongly lensed events detectable by next-generation GW detectors. In this work, we investigate the prospects of constraining the mass of the WDM particle using upcoming observations of the upgraded LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network. This requires a careful modeling of the detector selection effects. The upcoming fifth observing run (O5) is expected to yield only a modest bound, since only a few lensed pairs are expected at that early stage. By the sixth observing run (O6), we forecast a bound on the WDM particle mass, $m_{\rm wdm}^{-1} \lesssim 0.1$-$0.2\text{keV}^{-1}$ ($m_{\rm wdm} \gtrsim 5$-$10\text{keV}$), which is comparable to the tightest existing astrophysical constraints. Runs beyond O6 will tighten the constraint by roughly an order of magnitude. Strongly lensed GWs therefore offer a complementary, competitive, and independent probe of dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper forecasts the ability of upgraded LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observing runs to constrain warm dark matter (WDM) particle mass using strongly gravitationally lensed binary black hole merger signals; O6 is projected to yield competitive bounds (~5–10 keV), improving by ~an order of magnitude in later runs.
AI.motivation: Strongly lensed gravitational-wave transients encode information about lens mass distributions and redshifts, which depend on dark matter properties—particularly the free-streaming scale set by WDM particle mass. Current astrophysical constraints are tight but model-dependent; GW lensing offers a complementary, independent probe.
AI.method: Forecasts based on expected detection rates of strongly lensed BBH mergers in LVK’s O5 and O6 observing runs, incorporating realistic detector sensitivity, selection effects, lens population modeling (galaxies/clusters), and WDM-induced suppression of small-scale structure affecting lens abundance and time-delay distribution.
AI.result: O5 yields only weak constraints due to low lensed-event statistics; O6 forecasts a bound m_wdm ≳ 5–10 keV (i.e., m_wdm⁻¹ ≲ 0.1–0.2 keV⁻¹), comparable to best existing astrophysical limits; post-O6 runs improve this by ~an order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: Strongly lensed GWs constitute a competitive, independent, and complementary probe of WDM particle mass, with near-future LVK observations poised to deliver astrophysically significant constraints.

title: Di-hadron Fragmentation Functions beyond LO
