comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, Proceedings of DIS2026 (33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects), Bologna, Italy
summary: In this talk, we discuss the extraction of Dihadron Fragmentation Functions (DiFFs) beyond leading order. In particular, we review the latest extraction by the MAP Collaboration of the Unpolarized Dihadron Fragmentation Functions (DiFFs) from a fit of the 2017 BELLE data for the inclusive $π^+π^-$ pair production within the same jet in $e^+e^-$ annihilations. This new extraction improves the perturbative QCD accuracy by including NNLO calculations, relies on Monte Carlo generators only for flavor decomposition, and complements the traditional physics-informed parametrization with a Neural Network extraction. We also discuss the setup for the extraction of the transversely polarized DiFFs, where we revisit the NLO calculation for $e^+e^-$ annihilation into a transversely polarized quark-antiquark pair, obtaining a result different from the one reported in the literature.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an improved NNLO QCD extraction of unpolarized Dihadron Fragmentation Functions (DiFFs) from BELLE 2017 $e^+e^−$ data using hybrid physics-informed + neural network parametrization; it also identifies a discrepancy in the published NLO expression for transversely polarized DiFFs in $e^+e^−$ annihilation.
AI.motivation: To improve perturbative accuracy and modeling flexibility in extracting DiFFs—key nonperturbative inputs for spin-dependent hadronization studies—beyond leading order, especially for unpolarized and transversely polarized cases.
AI.method: Global fit to BELLE 2017 inclusive $π^+π^−$ pair production data in $e^+e^−$ collisions; employs NNLO pQCD calculations, uses Monte Carlo generators only for flavor decomposition (not for fragmentation modeling), and combines traditional analytic parametrization with a Neural Network ansatz for DiFFs; independently rederives the NLO cross section for transversely polarized quark-antiquark production.
AI.result: First NNLO-based extraction of unpolarized DiFFs with enhanced precision and reduced model dependence; neural network approach yields competitive fits without imposing strong functional forms; corrected NLO expression for transversely polarized DiFF observables, contradicting prior literature.
AI.conclusion: NNLO + machine learning enables more robust, less biased DiFF extractions; the revised NLO calculation implies previous extractions of transverse-spin DiFFs may be systematically biased, necessitating reanalysis.

title: Infrared Memory and Scrambling in a Dynamically Opened Coupled-SYK Majorana Junction
summary: We study a dynamically opened Majorana junction formed by two coupled Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) systems. A time-dependent bilinear coupling drives the system from a nearly decoupled to a strongly hybridized regime, providing an interacting realization of a Majorana shutter. Using a low-frequency analysis of the large-$N$ Keldysh theory around the conformal $q=4$ SYK saddle, we find that the opening retains a strong infrared memory, with the associated anomalous response becoming increasingly sensitive to the infrared cutoff. Exact finite-dimensional simulations of two $N=8$ SYK clusters show enhanced inter-sector entanglement, parity transfer, and cross-sector operator scrambling after the opening. These results connect the infrared structure of conformal SYK dynamics with finite-size many-body scrambling and show how a dynamically opened interacting Majorana system can retain long-wavelength memory beyond the quadratic limit.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a dynamically opened Majorana junction composed of two coupled Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev (SYK) systems, revealing persistent infrared memory and enhanced quantum scrambling during hybridization.
AI.motivation: To understand how interacting Majorana systems retain long-wavelength memory beyond the quadratic (non-interacting) limit, and to bridge conformal SYK infrared dynamics with finite-size many-body scrambling phenomena.
AI.method: Large-N Keldysh field theory analysis near the conformal q=4 SYK saddle, complemented by exact diagonalization simulations of two N=8 SYK clusters under time-dependent bilinear coupling.
AI.result: Low-frequency analysis shows strong infrared memory and increasing sensitivity of anomalous response to infrared cutoff; numerics reveal enhanced inter-sector entanglement, parity transfer, and cross-sector operator scrambling post-opening.
AI.conclusion: A dynamically opened interacting Majorana junction preserves long-wavelength memory rooted in SYK conformal structure, demonstrating that infrared physics governs finite-size scrambling and parity dynamics even in strongly hybridized regimes.

title: Probing Neutron Star Equation of State Universality with Gravitational Waves
summary: Current neutron star equation-of-state inferences assume that a common equation of state describes all neutron stars. However, {poorly understood dense-matter physics may give rise to distinct long-lived stellar subpopulations following different mass--tidal-deformability relations, invalidating this assumption. In this Letter, we demonstrate that next-generation gravitational-wave observatories enable neutron star equation-of-state universality to be transformed from an assumption into a testable hypothesis. By combining hierarchical Bayesian inference with a piecewise-polytropic parametrization of the neutron star equation of state, we establish a framework for testing equation-of-state universality with next-generation gravitational-wave observatories. We find that about 30 (50) loud binary neutron star mergers with network SNRs above 100 are sufficient to provide compelling evidence for departures from equation-of-state universality, even if only 20% (10%) of the population exhibits one of the representative non-universality parametrizations considered here.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a framework to test the universality of neutron star equations of state (EOS) using next-generation gravitational-wave observatories, showing that ~30–50 high-SNR binary neutron star mergers can robustly detect departures from EOS universality—even with only a small subpopulation exhibiting non-universal behavior.
AI.motivation: The common assumption that all neutron stars obey a single equation of state may be invalid due to poorly understood dense-matter physics potentially yielding distinct stellar subpopulations with different mass–tidal-deformability relations.
AI.method: Hierarchical Bayesian inference combined with a piecewise-polytropic EOS parametrization is used to construct a statistical framework for testing EOS universality in populations of binary neutron star mergers detected by future gravitational-wave observatories.
AI.result: Approximately 30 (50) loud binary neutron star mergers with network signal-to-noise ratios >100 are sufficient to provide compelling evidence against EOS universality—even if only 20% (10%) of the population follows a non-universal EOS parametrization.
AI.conclusion: EOS universality can be empirically tested—not merely assumed—with upcoming gravitational-wave data, transforming a foundational modeling assumption into a falsifiable hypothesis.

title: Global Fixed Point Potentials in the Abelian Higgs Model with $N$ flavors
summary: Existence of charged fixed points in the Abelian Higgs model with $N$ flavors in $d$ dimensions is studied using the functional renormalization group. We numerically solve the coupled fixed point equations for the scale dependent charge and the non-perturbative effective potential for the scalar field. We show that the $ε=4-d$ expansion, famously successful in theories with $O(N)$ symmetry, fails to produce reliable results when taking the $ε\rightarrow 1$ limit. By determining global fixed point potentials, it is shown that the critical flavor number at which charged fixed points appear, modifies significantly compared to the perturbative treatment. In $d=3$, signs of a richer fixed point structure with presumably multicritical fixed points are also found. Discussions include subtleties of the gauge fixing and the corresponding modified Ward-Takahashi identities, including the possibility of a nonzero dimensionless photon mass at the infrared fixed point.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates charged fixed points in the Abelian Higgs model with N flavors in d dimensions using functional renormalization group (FRG), revealing limitations of the ε-expansion and uncovering non-perturbative fixed point structure—including possible multicritical points in d=3 and implications of gauge fixing and modified Ward-Takahashi identities.
AI.motivation: To understand the existence and nature of charged fixed points in the Abelian Higgs model beyond perturbation theory, especially where standard ε = 4 − d expansion fails, and to assess non-perturbative effects on critical flavor number and infrared behavior including photon mass.
AI.method: Functional renormalization group (FRG) applied to the Abelian Higgs model with N scalar flavors; numerical solution of coupled flow equations for scale-dependent gauge charge and scalar effective potential; global analysis of fixed point potentials; careful treatment of gauge fixing and associated modified Ward-Takahashi identities.
AI.result: The ε-expansion breaks down as ε → 1; critical flavor number N_c for appearance of charged fixed points is significantly modified from perturbative predictions; in d = 3, evidence for richer fixed point structure including multicritical points; nonzero dimensionless photon mass possible at IR fixed point under certain gauge choices.
AI.conclusion: Charged fixed points in the Abelian Higgs model are intrinsically non-perturbative; FRG reveals qualitatively new physics beyond ε-expansion, with implications for gauge-Yukawa systems, conformal windows, and IR conformality in gauge-Higgs theories.

title: Decompactification and the Flat-Space Limit of AdS$_5\times$ S$^5$ Master Correlators
summary: We study the flat-space limit of AdS$_5$/CFT$_4$ holographic correlators while accounting for the simultaneous decompactification of the internal S$^5$. We show that this limit is naturally formulated in terms of master propagators and correlators, which resum the infinite tower of Kaluza--Klein modes. For boundary correlators, the resulting expressions can be interpreted in terms of amplitudes with kinematics restricted to 5d. We then consider master correlators whose external insertions are kept in the AdS$_5\times$S$^5$ bulk before taking the limit, and argue that they recover flat-space amplitudes with unrestricted kinematics in 10d Minkowski space. Finally, we show that the flat-space limit commutes with the boundary limit if we analytically continue the sphere so that the bulk geometry becomes AdS$_5 \times$dS$_5$, and the resulting formulae suggest an interpretation in terms of amplitudes in flat space with two time directions and with 10d kinematics satisfying two simultaneous null constraints. We discuss the implications of these constructions for flat-space holography and its relation to the Carrollian limit of the dual CFT.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the flat-space limit of AdS₅/CFT₄ correlators while simultaneously decompactifying the internal S⁵, introducing 'master propagators/correlators' that resum Kaluza–Klein modes; it shows boundary correlators reduce to 5d-restricted amplitudes, bulk master correlators recover full 10d flat-space amplitudes, and with AdS₅×dS₅ analytic continuation, the limits commute and suggest a 10d amplitude interpretation with two time directions and double null constraints—linking to Carrollian CFT and flat-space holography.
AI.motivation: To systematically derive flat-space scattering amplitudes from AdS/CFT by jointly taking the large-radius (flat-space) limit of AdS₅ and the decompactification limit of S⁵, resolving ambiguities in how Kaluza–Klein modes decouple and how bulk vs. boundary limits interplay.
AI.method: Uses master propagators and master correlators—generating functions that resum infinite Kaluza–Klein towers on S⁵—to organize the joint AdS₅→ℝ^{4,1} and S⁵→ℝ⁵ limit; employs analytic continuation to AdS₅×dS₅ to ensure commutativity of flat-space and boundary limits; interprets resulting structures via kinematic embeddings and null constraints in higher-dimensional Minkowski space.
AI.result: 1) Boundary master correlators yield 5d amplitudes with momenta constrained to a light-cone slice; 2) Bulk master correlators reproduce standard 10d flat-space amplitudes; 3) With AdS₅×dS₅ continuation, flat- and boundary-limits commute, yielding expressions interpretable as 10d amplitudes with signature (9,1) but subject to two independent null conditions—suggesting a 'bi-Carrollian' or double-null kinematic framework.
AI.conclusion: The flat-space limit of AdS₅×S⁵ holography is consistently captured by master correlators; the emergence of 10d amplitudes with dual null constraints points to a refined geometric realization of flat-space holography, intimately tied to the Carrollian structure of the decompactified CFT and offering new insight into the bulk reconstruction of scattering observables.

title: Spherically symmetric inextendibility of weak null singularities with Christoffel symbols in $L^s_{\text{loc}}$
summary: Motivated by the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in general relativity, we prove the inextendibility of spherically symmetric weak null singularities as spherically symmetric Lorentzian manifolds with a continuous metric and Christoffel symbols in $L^{s}_{\text{loc}}$ for $s>1$. The result assumes a suitable blow-up condition on the derivative of the area-radius function transverse to the weak null singularity in combination with a rigidity result on continuous spherically symmetric extensions across null boundaries proven in [1]. In particular we show that these assumptions are satisfied by the Reissner-Nordström-Vaidya spacetime as well as by a class of spacetimes arising from small and generic spherically symmetric perturbations of subextremal Reissner-Nordström under the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field system.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that spherically symmetric weak null singularities cannot be extended as Lorentzian manifolds with continuous metric and Christoffel symbols in L^s_loc (s > 1), under a transverse derivative blow-up condition and a rigidity result for continuous extensions; the result applies to Reissner-Nordström-Vaidya and generic small perturbations of subextremal Reissner-Nordström under Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field dynamics.
AI.motivation: To address the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in general relativity by establishing inextendibility of weak null singularities in spherically symmetric settings.
AI.method: Uses geometric analysis of spherically symmetric Lorentzian manifolds, leveraging a blow-up condition on the transverse derivative of the area-radius function and a rigidity theorem for continuous spherically symmetric extensions across null boundaries.
AI.result: Proves C^0-inextendibility of weak null singularities as spherically symmetric Lorentzian manifolds with continuous metric and Christoffel symbols in L^s_loc for s > 1; verifies assumptions for Reissner-Nordström-Vaidya and a class of dynamically formed spacetimes from small generic perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Under physically motivated regularity and blow-up conditions, spherically symmetric weak null singularities are inextendible — supporting strong cosmic censorship in this symmetry class.

title: Tracing Gluon Saturation through Hadronization at EIC
summary: Gluon saturation provides a window into the nonlinear nature of the strong interaction in nuclear matter. One direct consequence of saturation is the $\boldsymbol{k}_T$ broadening in the final state.We investigate how hadronization reshapes conventional signatures of gluon saturation at EIC within a complete event-generator framework. To this end, we implement in eHIJING an initial-state-radiation algorithm based on nonlinear small-$x$ evolution and complete the events with beam remnants, final-state radiation, and hadronization. In our simulations, the signal of parton-level nuclear $\boldsymbol{k}_T$ broadening is strongly diluted in both the nucleon energy correlator and leading-dihadron azimuthal decorrelation after hadronization. Global hadronic recoil, by contrast, remains sensitive to the underlying $\boldsymbol{k}_T$ broadening. We further demonstrate that Bayesian unfolding of the global hadronic recoil provides access to the underlying hard-scattering $\boldsymbol{k}_T$ distribution. These results establish the global hadronic recoil as a promising saturation observable at the EIC.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how hadronization affects signatures of gluon saturation—particularly k_T broadening—at the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), using the eHIJING event generator with a nonlinear small-x evolution-based initial-state radiation model. It finds that conventional observables (nucleon energy correlator, leading-dihadron azimuthal decorrelation) lose sensitivity to k_T broadening after hadronization, whereas global hadronic recoil retains sensitivity; Bayesian unfolding of this recoil recovers the underlying hard-scattering k_T distribution, establishing it as a robust saturation observable.
AI.motivation: To identify hadronic-level observables at the EIC that remain sensitive to gluon saturation effects—specifically parton-level k_T broadening—despite the distorting effects of hadronization, which typically dilutes conventional saturation signatures.
AI.method: Implemented a nonlinear small-x evolution–based initial-state radiation algorithm in eHIJING; completed events with beam remnants, final-state radiation, and string fragmentation hadronization; simulated and compared nuclear k_T broadening signals across multiple observables before and after hadronization; applied Bayesian unfolding to extract the underlying k_T distribution from global hadronic recoil.
AI.result: Parton-level k_T broadening signal is strongly diluted in nucleon energy correlator and leading-dihadron azimuthal decorrelation after hadronization; global hadronic recoil preserves clear sensitivity to the underlying k_T broadening; Bayesian unfolding successfully reconstructs the hard-scattering k_T distribution from recoil data.
AI.conclusion: Global hadronic recoil is a robust, hadron-level observable for gluon saturation at the EIC, uniquely resilient to hadronization effects and amenable to quantitative extraction of saturation-driven k_T broadening via Bayesian unfolding.

title: Cosmological Evolution of the Randall-Sundrum II Model with Running Vacuum: A Special Class of Solutions
summary: In this work, we construct a novel cosmological framework by integrating the running vacuum model into the Randall-Sundrum II braneworld scenario. We derive a special class of analytical solutions in the model. Our investigation focuses on the complete evolutionary trajectory of the universe, with particular emphasis on the realization of primordial inflation and the evolution of cosmic entropy. We evaluate the model's viability across three scenarios: dust-dominated, radiation-dominated, and general perfect fluid-dominated universes. Our findings show that while the hybrid model is in principle capable of supporting inflation, producing enough e-fold number demands either severe fine-tuning of the parameter or unreasonably large (and thus physically unnatural) value of the parameter.

AI.tldr: This paper combines the running vacuum model with the Randall-Sundrum II braneworld to construct a novel cosmological framework, deriving analytical solutions and assessing its ability to support primordial inflation and cosmic entropy evolution across dust-, radiation-, and general fluid-dominated scenarios; it finds inflation is possible in principle but requires extreme fine-tuning or unphysical parameter values.
AI.motivation: To explore whether a hybrid cosmological model—combining the running vacuum model and the Randall-Sundrum II braneworld—can self-consistently realize primordial inflation and describe the full cosmic evolutionary trajectory, including entropy dynamics.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of cosmological solutions within the integrated running vacuum–RSII framework; systematic evaluation of inflationary viability (e-fold number) under dust-, radiation-, and general perfect fluid-dominated assumptions.
AI.result: A special class of analytical solutions is obtained; the hybrid model supports inflation in principle, but achieving sufficient e-folds requires either extreme fine-tuning or physically unnatural parameter magnitudes.
AI.conclusion: The running vacuum–RSII model is theoretically viable but observationally and physically challenged for realistic inflationary cosmology due to severe parameter sensitivity.

title: Fast Bayesian Inference for Long-Duration Gravitational-Wave Signals in 3G detectors
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Supplemental PDF file included as ancilliary material
summary: Third-generation (3G) gravitational-wave detectors will observe binary-neutron-star inspirals for nearly a day, so Earth's rotation becomes part of the signal rather than a negligible correction. This destroys the usual separation between intrinsic and extrinsic parameters and creates a major computational bottleneck for Bayesian inference. We show that the exact five-harmonic Jaranowski-Krolak-Schutz (JKS) decomposition restores the separation of the rotating antenna amplitude response from the computationally expensive intrinsic waveform calculations. By sampling the intrinsic waveform on a frequency grid set by its phase curvature and then applying error-controlled relative binning, likelihood evaluations for a 21.3-h signal are accelerated by O(10^4), making day-long 3G signal inference practical.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an efficient method for Bayesian inference of binary-neutron-star inspiral signals in third-generation gravitational-wave detectors by restoring parameter separation via the exact five-harmonic JKS decomposition and accelerating likelihood evaluation using phase-curvature–based sampling and error-controlled relative binning.
AI.motivation: Earth's rotation during long-duration (e.g., ~21.3 h) binary-neutron-star inspiral signals in 3G detectors breaks the standard intrinsic–extrinsic parameter separation, causing severe computational bottlenecks in Bayesian inference.
AI.method: The authors employ the exact five-harmonic Jaranowski-Krolak-Schutz (JKS) decomposition to decouple the rotating antenna response (extrinsic) from the intrinsic waveform; they sample the intrinsic waveform on a frequency grid determined by its phase curvature and apply error-controlled relative binning to accelerate likelihood evaluation.
AI.result: Likelihood evaluations for a 21.3-hour signal are accelerated by a factor of O(10^4), rendering day-long Bayesian inference computationally feasible for 3G detectors.
AI.conclusion: The exact JKS decomposition combined with adaptive frequency sampling and relative binning restores computational tractability for long-duration GW signal inference without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Nonlinear evolution in Galileon EFTs: Regularization and screening
summary: In a scalar effective field theory (EFT) with Galileon symmetry, we distinguish the strong-field expansion from the derivative expansion and study spherically symmetric classical nonlinear dynamics. More concretely, we consider two models related via perturbative field redefinitions: one with second-order equations that can also exhibit screening, and one that includes a higher-derivative term that introduces a propagating ghost. The latter term is of the type that can ``regularise'' the equations to render them well-posed as an initial value problem. For initial data that respect the derivative expansion, we find that the first model (ghost-free, unregularised) develops ill-posed regions during evolution only when the derivative expansion breaks down. This result persists in the strong-field regime. We further find that the regularized model reproduces the evolution of the unregularised one when the latter remains well-posed, while it exhibits tachyonic behaviour when the unregularised one becomes ill-posed. We also consider initial data that corresponds to stationary states that exhibit screening in the unregularised, ghost-free theory. In this case, we find that the regularised theory can remain well-posed for initial data that the unregularised one developed ill-posed regions. However, the ghost term naturally dominates over the Galileon term in the screening regime, contrary to common expectation.

AI.tldr: This paper compares two scalar EFT models with Galileon symmetry—one ghost-free but potentially ill-posed, and one higher-derivative 'regularized' model containing a ghost—analyzing their spherically symmetric classical dynamics. It shows that ill-posedness arises only when the derivative expansion breaks down, even in strong-field regimes; the regularized model agrees with the ghost-free one where the latter is well-posed, but exhibits tachyonic behavior otherwise; unexpectedly, the ghost term dominates in screening configurations.
AI.motivation: To clarify the relationship between strong-field and derivative expansions in Galileon EFTs, and to assess whether higher-derivative 'regularization' meaningfully improves well-posedness without violating physical consistency (e.g., ghost/tachyon emergence).
